subtitle: Unsung Hands of India’s Everyday Healing

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle village wide at dusk
panels.action: A Nai Surgeon sharpens a razor beside a village well while a Dai Midwife walks past with a cloth bundle of tools; behind them, mud houses, a banyan tree and a distant temple glow in fading light.

dialogue.text: In an age of Sanskrit verses and royal physicians, it was Nai surgeons and dai midwives who touched most bodies, healing in the shadows of a world that would not write their names.

i18n.hi: संस्कृत श्लोकों और राजवैद्यों के दौर में, ज़्यादातर जिस्मों को नै और दाइयाँ ही छूती थीं, एक ऐसे साए में जहाँ किसी ने उनके नाम तक नहीं लिखे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on palm-leaf manuscript on a scholar’s desk
panels.action: A learned Brahmin physician in simple robes sits cross-legged indoors, hand poised over a palm-leaf manuscript as an apprentice holds a lamp, the etched lines of a medical treatise visible on the leaf.

dialogue.text: The Charaka Samhita and Sushruta Samhita spoke of ideal students: disciplined, pure, well-born enough to guard the honour of the art. Their words defined who should learn, and whom to avoid.

i18n.hi: चरक संहिता और सुश्रुत संहिता के आदर्श शिष्य थे अनुशासित, शुद्ध, खानदानी – जो विद्या की इज़्ज़त बचा सकें। इन्हीं शब्दों ने तय किया कौन सीखे, और किसे दूर रखा जाए।

panels.shot: high-angle interior wide of gurukula courtyard
panels.action: Inside a forest gurukula, a small group of young men of visibly high status sit before a teacher under a tree, while at the gate, two poorly dressed youths stand uncertainly, held back by a silent servant.

dialogue.text: Some verses praised the physician who shunned patients from despised groups, or refused the ill whose suffering might stain his reputation. Law books echoed this, tying healing to ritual rank.

i18n.hi: कुछ श्लोक उस वैद्य की तारीफ़ करते हैं जो नीची कही जाने वाली जातियों के रोगी टाल दे, या उन बीमारों से मुँह मोड़ ले जिनका दुख उसकी इज़्ज़त पर दाग समझा जाए। कानून भी यही दोहराते, इलाज को पूजा और दर्जे से बाँधते।

panels.shot: dynamic split composition, half showing ritual elite care, half showing crowded village lane
panels.action: On one side, a wealthy man reclines on a cot as a priest-physician examines him in a calm veranda; on the other side, a narrow village lane teems with farmers, artisans, women and children, many clearly weary and ill.

dialogue.text: Yet most bodies did not belong to kings, merchants, or brahmins. They belonged to ploughmen, weavers, potters, widows, labourers, outcasts, and women whose births and deaths never reached the manuscripts.

i18n.hi: लेकिन ज़्यादातर जिस्म राजा, बनिये या ब्राह्मण के नहीं थे। वे हलवाहों, बुनकरों, कुम्हारों, विधवाओं, मज़दूरों, बहिष्कृतों और उन औरतों के थे जिनके जनम‑मौत कभी पांडुलिपियों तक नहीं पहुँचे।

panels.shot: medium shot at a village barber’s shade
panels.action: Under a thatched awning, a Nai Surgeon trims a farmer’s beard with a razor while, on a nearby mat, his kit lies open: small knives, tweezers, a cautery rod, thread, and herbs in cloth packets.

dialogue.text: Here the Nai, the village barber-surgeon, plied his trade. With the same steady hand that shaved cheeks, he lanced boils, stitched gashes, set simple fractures and drained pus from swollen limbs.

i18n.hi: यहीं नै, गाँव का हजाम‑सर्जन, अपना काम करता था। वही हाथ जो दाढ़ी बनाते, फोड़े चीरते, ज़ख्म सीते, छोटी हड्डियाँ जोड़ते और सूजी हुई नसों से मवाद निकालते।

panels.shot: close-up on Nai Surgeon’s weathered hands
panels.action: The Nai Surgeon’s rough hands grip a villager’s arm, gently holding a small knife over a swollen abscess as another man looks away, anxious, under the shade of a tree.

dialogue.text: His training was not from Charaka’s polished verses. It came from fathers and uncles, from watching, risking, failing and learning, from a thousand small operations in lanes and courtyards.

i18n.hi: उसकी तालीम चरक के चाँदी जैसे श्लोकों से नहीं आई। वह बाप‑चाचा से, देखते‑देखते, जान जोखिम में डालते, गलती कर सीखते, गली‑मुहल्लों में हज़ार छोटे ऑपरेशनों से आई।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot in dim hut
panels.action: Inside a dim mud house lit by a single oil lamp, a Dai Midwife kneels by a labouring woman, hands steady on the woman’s belly, while other women support the mother and a child peeks from behind a curtain.

dialogue.text: And when labour pains ripped through the night, it was the dai who came. Village midwives, often from marginalised castes, caught most babies into the world, unseen by the Sanskrit authors.

i18n.hi: और जब रात को प्रसव पीड़ा चीखती, तो दाई आती थी। गाँव की दाइयाँ, अक्सर हाशिए की जातियों से, ज़्यादातर बच्चों को दुनिया में लातीं, उन संस्कृत लेखकों की नज़र से दूर।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder close-up from behind the dai
panels.action: From behind the Dai Midwife’s shoulder, we see her tying a cord with practiced ease, her face calm as the exhausted mother clutches a rope hung from the ceiling beam.

dialogue.text: “Breathe, sister. Many have walked this edge. We will cross it too.”

i18n.hi: "साँस ले बहन। कितनी इस किनारे से गुज़री हैं। हम भी पार जाएँगे।"

panels.shot: wide shot of village square with multiple healers
panels.action: In a village square, different practitioners attend to people: a bonesetter manipulates a man’s arm, a forest healer displays roots and barks, and a snake-charmer-like figure holds a basket while villagers listen intently.

dialogue.text: Around them moved bonesetters who knew the language of joints, poison healers who tracked bites and toxins, and forest herbalists whose plants never appeared in any royal physician’s list.

i18n.hi: इनके आस‑पास हड्डी जोड़ने वाले घूमते, जो जोड़‑मोड़ की ज़ुबान जानते थे; ज़हरगुन जो काट‑डंस और ज़हर पहचानते; और जंगल वैद्य, जिनकी जड़ी‑बूटियाँ किसी राजवैद्य की सूची में नहीं थीं।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of rural landscape with a distant walled town
panels.action: From above, a patchwork of fields and hamlets stretches to the horizon, with a walled town a long way off; a thin path winds from village to town, dotted with a solitary traveller.

dialogue.text: For many, the nearest formally trained physician was days away. Archaeologists reading old skeletons find signs of untreated disease and injury, but also of bones that healed, hinting at care beyond the elite clinics.

i18n.hi: कई लोगों के लिए, नियम से पढ़ा‑लिखा वैद्य कई दिन की दूरी पर था। पुरानी हड्डियाँ पढ़ते पुरातत्वविद कभी‑कभी अधूरे रोग और चोट के निशान पाते हैं, पर साथ ही जुड़ी हुई हड्डियाँ भी, जो ऊँचे दर्जे की हकीमी से बाहर की देखभाल दिखाती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Brahmin physician turning away a supplicant
panels.action: In a town veranda, a Brahmin physician in clean white cloth listens as a poorly dressed man pleads with folded hands; the physician’s face is conflicted as he gestures the man away while a household elder watches.

dialogue.text: Texts and law codes sometimes warned healers against treating outcastes, enemies, or those whose touch was said to pollute. In practice, this meant some doors closed when the poor and despised knocked.

i18n.hi: शास्त्र और कानून कभी‑कभी वैद्यों को बहिष्कृतों, दुश्मनों या ‘छूत’ कहे जाने वालों का इलाज न करने की ताकीद करते थे। असल में, इसका मतलब था कि ग़रीब और ठुकराए जब दरवाज़ा खटखटाएँ तो कुछ चौखटें बंद रहें।

panels.shot: contrast shot: foreground non-elite healers at work, background faint outline of temple and manuscript
panels.action: In the foreground under a tree, a Nai Surgeon bandages a boy’s head while the Dai Midwife soothes his mother; in the hazy background, a temple spire and a faint silhouette of a scholar with a manuscript are barely visible.

dialogue.text: When elite healers hesitated or stayed distant, village hands stepped in. Caste and gender lines shaped who could enter the Sanskrit schools; they did not stop bodies from falling sick or needing touch.

i18n.hi: जब ऊँचे वैद्य झिझके या दूर रहे, गाँव के हाथ आगे बढ़े। जाति और जेंडर ने तय किया किसे संस्कृत गुरुकुल में घुसने दिया जाएगा; बीमार पड़ने और छू कर इलाज की ज़रूरत पर उनका बस नहीं था।

panels.shot: close-up of a palm-leaf manuscript margin next to a barber’s tools
panels.action: On a simple wooden floor, a palm-leaf manuscript lies half-unrolled beside a barber’s razor and a midwife’s cloth pouch; only the tools are worn from heavy use, the manuscript edges still crisp.

dialogue.text: Modern historians speak of braided sciences. Palms of texts and hands of practice were woven together, even if the strands did not meet as equals or share the same honour in memory.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार इसे गुंथी हुई विद्या कहते हैं। शास्त्र की हथेलियाँ और मेहनत के हाथ आपस में बुने थे, भले ही वे बराबरी पर न मिलते हों या याद में एक‑सा मान न पाते हों।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a modern scholar in an archive
panels.action: A present-day researcher in simple clothes sits in an archive, leafing through fragile manuscripts and field notes, while sketches of village healers and photographs of tools are spread across the desk.

dialogue.text: Recent work, from bone studies to village histories, has begun to trace these hidden practitioners, piecing them back into the story that once focused almost only on Sanskrit and courts.

i18n.hi: नई खोजें, हड्डियों की जाँच से लेकर गाँवों की कहानियों तक, इन गुमनाम हकीमों के रास्ते खोज रही हैं, उन्हें उस कहानी में जोड़ रही हैं जो अब तक बस संस्कृत और दरबारों पर टिक गई थी।

panels.shot: twilight wide shot of village lane with multiple generations
panels.action: At twilight in the same village lane, an older Nai Surgeon watches a younger apprentice shave a client while a middle-aged Dai Midwife teaches a teenage girl to tie a cloth bundle of tools; children play nearby.

dialogue.text: Their knowledge travelled not through examinations or royal patronage, but through apprenticeships, marriages, whispers, and work. It lasted for centuries, even as formal curricula rose and fell.

i18n.hi: इनका ज्ञान न तो परीक्षाओं से चला, न ही राजाश्रय से। यह चेला‑गिरी, शादियों, कानाफूसी और काम से बहा। सदियों तक टिका रहा, जबकि बड़े पाठ्यक्रम उठे और गिर गए।

panels.shot: close-up on Dai Midwife and Nai Surgeon looking directly toward viewer
panels.action: The Nai Surgeon and Dai Midwife stand side by side in a quiet moment, faces lined and steady, gazing outward as if at the reader; behind them, the village stretches into the distance.

dialogue.text: To remember the history of healing in India is to name their hands too, and to see how law, caste and gender once decided whose pain reached the page and whose stayed only in the dust of the street.

i18n.hi: भारत में इलाज की कहानी याद करना मतलब इनके हाथों को भी नाम देना, और देखना कि कैसे कानून, जाति और जेंडर ने तय किया किसका दर्द किताब में आएगा और किसका धूल में ही घुल जाएगा।

title_i18n.hi: हजाम सर्जन और गाँव की दाइयाँ

subtitle_i18n.en: Unsung Hands of India’s Everyday Healing
subtitle_i18n.hi: भारत की रोज़मर्रा की ठंडी इलाज‑कारी हथेलियाँ
